suggestions.suggestion: Assert high Quality of Service (QoS=8 to 11) on Master 2 while low QoS traffic is active on Master 1 to test priority preemption.
test_outline: 1. Start steady stream of low QoS (QoS=2) traffic on Master 1
2. Issue high priority read transaction (QoS=10) on Master 2 to contending slave port
3. Measure arbitration grant latency to verify Master 2 gets preemptive grant
4. Verify high QoS transaction completes ahead of pending Master 1 requests
suggestions.reasoning: Low and normal QoS traffic are covered. Programming master QoS registers to range [8:11] exercises the higher tiers of multi-level priority arbiters.

suggestions.suggestion: Issue highest emergency QoS level transactions (QoS=15) during crossbar bandwidth saturation.
test_outline: 1. Saturate all interconnect slave ports with concurrent normal transactions
2. Inject single emergency write transaction with AxQOS = 4'b1111 (qos_urgent)
3. Check that arbiter immediately halts lower priority scheduling and routes urgent packet
4. Validate zero cycle starvation on urgent channel
suggestions.reasoning: Urgent QoS (12-15) is designed for real-time display/camera subsystem traffic. Simply requires setting AxQOS[3:0] >= 12 on the master interface.

suggestions.suggestion: Drive an AXI4 maximum allowable burst length (AxLEN=255, 256 beats) across crossbar to verify interconnect beat counter rollover.
test_outline: 1. Configure master VIP to issue INCR write burst with AxLEN=255
2. Target high-throughput slave memory port
3. Verify interconnect propagates all 256 beats without stall or lost data beats
4. Check WLAST and BVALID handshakes match protocol compliance
dependencies: Slave VIP configured with deep burst buffer
suggestions.reasoning: Short (2-8) and medium (9-64) bursts are covered. 256-beat bursts test crossbar data buffer FIFO depth and internal credit counters at maximum capacity.

suggestions.suggestion: Issue AXI cacheline WRAP4, WRAP8, and WRAP16 read bursts targeted at slave cache memory.
test_outline: 1. Set master VIP AxBURST to 2'b10 (WRAP) with AxLEN = 3, 7, and 15
2. Align start address within cache line boundary
3. Verify slave return beats wrap correctly to lower boundary
4. Check crossbar address generation unit preserves wrap boundary
dependencies: Slave memory model supporting wrapping addresses
suggestions.reasoning: Fixed and INCR bursts have thousands of hits, but wrap bursts require specific burst length (2, 4, 8, 16) and aligned addresses, typically generated by CPU cache controllers.

suggestions.suggestion: Program slave VIP responder to return SLVERR on address access to protected peripheral aperture.
test_outline: 1. Configure slave peripheral VIP error callback to assert RRESP=2'b10 (SLVERR)
2. Issue master read transaction to peripheral address
3. Verify interconnect passes SLVERR back to the initiating master without dropping channel
4. Check interconnect error logging status register
dependencies: Slave VIP error injection callback support
suggestions.reasoning: OKAY and EXOKAY are covered under normal operations. SLVERR requires either slave VIP error configuration or attempting an illegal access to a slave register.

suggestions.suggestion: Drive master transactions to unmapped address holes in interconnect address map to trigger internal default slave DECERR.
test_outline: 1. Identify unmapped holes in interconnect address decode table
2. Master VIP sends write request to unmapped address 0xDEAD_0000
3. Verify internal default slave responds with BRESP=2'b11 (DECERR)
4. Ensure bus pipeline drains cleanly and crossbar remains operational
dependencies: Knowledge of interconnect system memory map
suggestions.reasoning: DECERR is generated by the crossbar's internal error responder when no slave port matches the requested address decoding window.

suggestions.suggestion: Configure slave agent to permanently withhold BVALID/RVALID handshake and verify crossbar protocol watchdog timer triggers timeout.
test_outline: 1. Set interconnect bus timeout counter register to 256 cycles
2. Master issues read request to Slave 3
3. Force Slave 3 VIP to withhold ARREADY or RVALID indefinitely
4. Verify interconnect raises timeout interrupt, terminates transaction with DECERR, and unblocks arbiter
dependencies: Slave VIP unresponsive stall mode capability
suggestions.reasoning: Watchdog timeout protects against system lockup caused by unresponsive third-party IP cores. Requires artificial slave stalling.
